{"title": "The Dino Team by the Sea", "level": 2, "topic": "dinosaurs", "target_skill": "vowel_teams", "text": "Maya reads a big book about dinosaurs. The book says new facts are found each day!

She reads about a dino team by the sea. The team can leap and sail and float.

One dino eats green leaves. She has a long neck. She reaches up high to eat the leaves in the trees.

One dino likes to swim. He floats in the sea like a boat. His tail makes a big wave.

One dino has a sail on his back. It soaks up heat from the sun. Then he feels warm!

Rain falls on the sea. The dino team runs to a cave. They wait for the rain to stop.

Soon the sun peeks out. The team eats a meal of leaves and beans.

Maya shuts her book. "What a team!" she says. "I will read more each day."", "cover_scene": "Three friendly dinosaurs on a sunny beach by the sea, one with a long neck eating leaves, one floating in the waves, and one with a tall sail on its back."}

{"title": "Rain on the Dino Trail", "level": 2, "topic": "dinosaurs", "target_skill": "vowel_teams", "text": "Maya and Dad take a trail to the dino hall. New facts wait for them there!

Rain drips on the trail. Maya wears a coat. The rain makes a dark stain on the road.

In the hall, a big dino stands tall. Its tail is long. Its teeth are neat and sharp.

Maya reads the sign. "This dino ate meat. It ate a lot each day!"

Next, she sees a dino with a beak. It ate seeds and leaves. It made a nest and sat on eggs.

A man shows Maya a big bone. "Feel it," he says. The bone feels cold.

Maya draws a dino on a sheet. She paints it green with a red tail.

The rain ends. The sun beams on the road home.

"That was a great day!" Maya says. "Can we come again?"

Dad grins. "Yes. Soon."", "cover_scene": "A girl in a yellow raincoat and her dad walking a wet path toward a museum with a huge dinosaur skeleton visible through tall windows."}

{"title": "The Dino Egg in the Oak Tree", "level": 2, "topic": "dinosaurs", "target_skill": "vowel_teams", "text": "Maya finds a big egg near an oak tree. It is by the train track.

"Is it real?" she says. The egg has a crack.

Out pops a tiny dino! It has green skin and a long tail.

"I will call you Oat," Maya says.

Oat eats leaves from the oak tree. He eats beans. He eats a peach!

Maya reads a book to Oat. Facts about dinosaurs fill each page.

"Long ago, some dinos ate meat. Some ate seeds and leaves like you," she reads.

Oat needs a home. Maya makes a nest of hay near the road.

Rain falls. Oat sleeps in his nest. Maya keeps him dry with a coat.

In the morning, Oat is bigger! His feet are huge.

Maya gives a big squeal. "Soon you will not fit in this nest!"

Oat licks her cheek.", "cover_scene": "A girl kneeling beside a cracked speckled egg under a big oak tree as a tiny green baby dinosaur peeks out."}
Noted.

{"title": "Oat and the Boat Race", "level": 2, "topic": "dinosaurs", "target_skill": "vowel_teams", "text": "Oat the dino is big now. He can pull a boat!

Maya paints the boat green. She paints a tail on each side.

"Ready to race?" she calls.

Oat nods. He steps in the lake. The road of waves goes far.

Maya reads the rules out loud. "Stay in your lane. Wait for the beep."

Beep! The boats go. Oat kicks his feet. Spray soaks Maya's coat.

A red boat takes the lead. Maya feels sad.

Then a gust of wind fills the sail. Oat leaps! The green boat speeds up.

They reach the last float. Oat gives one big kick.

The green boat wins by a nose!

The team cheers. Maya gets a gold seal on a sheet of paper.

She reads it to Oat. "First place!"

Oat eats a peach to feast. Maya eats one too.", "cover_scene": "A large friendly green dinosaur pulling a small painted boat with a girl aboard across a sparkling lake, other boats behind."}
Noted.

{"title": "Oat Paints the Dino Road", "title_note": "", "level": 2, "topic": "dinosaurs", "target_skill": "vowel_teams", "text": "Maya has a plan. She will make a dino road!

She gets paint. Red paint. Gray paint. A pail of white paint too.

Oat helps. He dips his tail in the pail. Then he paints the road!

The road goes past the oak tree. It goes past the lake. It goes past the goat pen.

Maya nails a sign by the road. She reads it out loud. "Dino Road. Stay in your lane!"

Soon a toad hops on the road. A snail creeps on the road. The goat walks on the road.

"Wait!" Maya calls. "This road is for dinos!"

Oat gives a big roar. But then he smiles.

"You may all come," Maya says. "Dinos like to share."

So the toad and the snail and the goat ride on Oat's back, down the long gray road.", "cover_scene": "A big green dinosaur dipping its tail in a paint pail to paint a winding road, with a goat, a snail, and a toad watching."}

{"title": "Oat and the Deep Cave", "level": 2, "topic": "dinosaurs", "target_skill": "vowel_teams", "text": "Maya reads a new dino fact. "Some bones hide in deep caves!"

"Let's go, Oat," she says.

They take the gray road. They pass the oak tree. They reach a deep cave by the sea.

Inside it is dim. Maya holds a light. Oat keeps close.

Drip. Drip. Water leaks from the peak of the cave.

Then Maya sees it. A huge bone in the clay!

"Wait," she says. "Is this real?"

She brushes the clay away. The bone is long and pale.

Oat sniffs it. He gives a soft moan.

"Do not be sad," Maya says. "This dino lived long ago. Now she can teach us."

They place the bone in a crate. They haul it up the trail.

At home, Maya makes a neat sign: MAYA'S BONE.

Oat beams. What a team!", "cover_scene": "A girl holding a lantern beside a green dinosaur inside a dim rocky cave, a huge pale bone half buried in clay."}

{"title": "The Dino Fair on Main Street", "level": 2, "topic": "dinosaurs", "target_skill": "vowel_teams", "text": "A dino fair comes to Main Street! Maya and Oat go at dawn.

Booths fill the street. One booth has dino art. One booth has games. One booth sells sweet treats.

Maya reads a fact card out loud. "New dino facts are found each year!"

At the first booth, Maya paints a dino. She paints it teal with a gold tail.

At the next booth, she throws a ball at a stack of cans. She beats the game! She wins a toy dino.

Oat waits by the treat cart. He wants a snack.

Maya buys him oats and a peach. Oat eats it all in one gulp!

Then a man calls, "Who can roar the best?"

Oat takes a deep breath. ROAR!

The whole street claps. Oat wins a big blue sash.

What a neat day!", "cover_scene": "A busy street fair with colorful booths, dinosaur banners, a girl holding a toy dinosaur, and a big green dinosaur wearing a blue sash."}

{"title": "Oat and the Night Sky Dino", "level": 2, "topic": "dinosaurs", "target_skill": "vowel_teams", "text": "Maya reads a new fact. "Some stars make shapes in the night sky!"

"Let's look, Oat," she says.

They wait for dark. They take a quilt to the green field by the oak tree.

The sky is deep blue. Then black. Stars peek out, one by one.

Maya sees three bright stars in a row. "That is a tail!" she says.

She traces more stars. A neck. A head. A row of teeth!

"Oat, it is a sky dino!"

Oat lifts his snout and gives a soft roar. The stars seem to gleam back.

A streak zooms past. A shooting star!

"Make a wish," Maya says.

She shuts her eyes tight. She wishes for more days like this one.

Oat leans close. Maya leans on his warm side.

Soon both of them sleep, under the sky dino.", "cover_scene": "A girl and a big green dinosaur lying on a quilt in a dark grassy field, gazing at stars that form a dinosaur shape."}

{"title": "Oat and the Shell Shop", "level": 2, "topic": "dinosaurs", "target_skill": "digraphs", "text": "Maya and Oat check the beach. They wish to find shells.

The shop by the dock sells dino things. A chart of dino facts hangs in the shop. Maya reads it. "New dino facts show up each year!"

"May we shop?" Maya asks.

The shop man grins. "Pick a thing that you wish for."

Maya picks a white shell. It has a shine like a tooth.

Oat shoves his snout in a dish of chips. Crunch! He chomps them all.

"Oat!" Maya says. "You must share!"

Oat shuts his mouth. He looks shy.

Then Oat digs in the sand with his chin. He finds a shell! It is thick and pink.

He puts it in Maya's hand.

"Thank you," Maya says. "This shell is the best."

They march home as the sun sinks.", "cover_scene": "A girl and a green dinosaur beside a small seaside shop filled with shells, the dinosaur nosing a thick pink shell into her hand."}

{"title":"Oat Meets the Octopus","level":2,"topic":"sea dinosaurs","target_skill":"digraphs","text":"Maya and Oat go to the fish tank hall.

A big glass tank shines. Maya puts her chin on the glass.

Then she sees it. An octopus! It has eight long arms.

"Wow!" Maya says. "It can shift its shape. It can squish in a thin gap!"

The octopus shoots past. It grabs a shell with one arm.

Oat taps the glass with his snout. The octopus turns pink!

Maya reads a chart on the wall. "Long ago, huge sea beasts swam here. Some had fins and sharp teeth. New facts come each year!"

She shows Oat a sketch of one. It looks much like a dino with flippers.

"You had cousins in the sea," she says.

Oat gives a soft huff.

The octopus waves one arm. Maya waves back.

"Thank you," she whispers. "What a day!"","cover_scene":"A girl and a green dinosaur pressing close to a glowing aquarium tank where a pink octopus spreads its eight arms."}

{"title":"Five Sea Giants","level":2,"topic":"sea dinosaurs","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya sees a show. It tells about five huge beasts in the sea, long ago.

The first one has a long neck. It eats fish. It sails in the deep sea like a boat.

The next one has a wide tail. It beats the waves. It leaps and lands with a big splash.

The third one is a speedy one. It streaks past like a train. It reaches for a meal.

The fourth one has teeth like nails. Maya peeks from her seat. "Yikes!"

The last one is the biggest. It is as long as a road! Its jaw can eat a whole seal.

Maya reads the last screen. "These beasts lived in the sea. Each one was real!"

Oat leans on Maya.

"Do not be afraid," she says. "They swam here long ago."","cover_scene":"Five enormous prehistoric sea creatures swimming in deep blue ocean water, with long necks, flippers, and big tails."}

{"title":"Dr. Scott and the Sea Reptiles","level":2,"topic":"marine reptiles","target_skill":"digraphs","text":"Maya watches a show with Dr. Scott. He digs up bones and shares what he finds.

"Long ago, big reptiles filled the oceans," he says. "They lived when dinosaurs did."

The screen shows one with a thin neck. It shoots through the water like a dart.

{"title":"Oat and the Sea Animal Team","level":2,"topic":"sea animals","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Oat wants a team. He roars, "Who will join me?"

A sea turtle floats by. "I will!" she says. She can glide for miles and hold her breath a long time.

A shark speeds up. "I will!" he says. He has rows of teeth and never needs sleep.

An octopus creeps from a crack. "I will!" she says. She has eight arms and three hearts!

A croc waits in the reeds. "I will!" he snaps. He can stay still for days.

Oat grins. "Now we are a real team."

They race down the coast. The turtle leads. The shark keeps pace. The octopus rides on Oat's back.

Maya waits on the beach with a pail of treats.

"Great job, team!" she calls.

Each one gets a snack. Oat gets seaweed. The team eats by the sea until the sun goes down.","cover_scene":"A green dinosaur swimming at the head of a line of sea animals - a turtle, a shark, an octopus, and a crocodile - along a sunny coast."}

{"title":"Tail First! A Dolphin Day","level":3,"topic":"dolphins","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya reads an amazing ocean fact out loud: "Dolphins are born tail first!"

"Tail first?" she says. "Let's go see, Oat."

They sail out in a small boat on a calm, gray sea. Oat keeps his snout low, waiting.

Soon a sleek dolphin leaps beside them, and then another. They squeak and chirp, speaking in sounds too high for Maya to hear.

One dolphin swims slowly near the boat. She is huge and round.

"Wait," Maya breathes. "I think she is a mom."

The sea churns. Then Maya sees it — a tiny tail! The baby slides out tail first, then floats up for its first gulp of air.

"That way it will not breathe too soon," Maya explains to Oat.

The team of dolphins sweeps away. Maya waves until they reach the deep.

"Best day at sea," she says.","cover_scene":"A girl and a green dinosaur leaning over the side of a small boat while a mother dolphin and her newborn calf surface in gray-blue waves."}

{"title":"The Dolphin Who Knew Her Name","level":3,"topic":"dolphins","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya reads that each dolphin makes its own whistle soon after it is born. That whistle is like a name!

"Oat, they call each other by name," she says.

They row out at daybreak. The sea is clear and green.

A sleek dolphin appears. She squeaks and squawks. Then she leaps — so high she seems to hang in the air!

Another dolphin slaps its tail on the sea. Smack! Water sprays across the boat and soaks Oat's snout.

A third blows a stream of bubbles that float up like beads.

"They are speaking," Maya explains. "Leaping and slapping mean things too."

Maya cups her hands and makes her own sound — a long, low peep.

The first dolphin repeats it back, nearly the same!

Maya beams. "She learned my name."

Oat gives a deep roar, and the dolphins reply.","cover_scene":"Three bottlenose dolphins leaping, tail-slapping, and blowing bubbles around a small rowboat holding a girl and a green dinosaur at sunrise."}

{"title":"The Pod and the Bright Blue Net","level":3,"topic":"dolphins","target_skill":"blends","text":"Maya learns that dolphins live in groups called pods. A baby dolphin is a calf, and it stays close to its mom.

She and Oat glide out in the small boat. A pod swims past, sleek and swift. They splash and spin and slap their tails.

"Dolphins are not fish," Maya tells Oat. "They are mammals, like us. They breathe air."

A dolphin clicks. The sound streams out, strikes a stone, and skips back. That is how she finds her food in the gloom.

Then Maya spots trouble. A bright blue net drifts near the pod! A small calf swims straight at it.

"Stop!" Maya cries.

Oat plunges in. He grips the net with his strong snout and drags it free.

The calf twists away and spins with glee.

The pod claps the sea with their flippers. Splash! Splash! Splash!","cover_scene":"A green dinosaur in the water pulling a tangled blue net away from a small dolphin calf while a girl cheers from a boat."}

{"title":"Oat and the Rocket Roar","level":3,"topic":"rockets","target_skill":"blends","text":"Maya learns a loud fact: a rocket blasting off is louder than thunder!

"Let's go, Oat," she says. They stand on the grass and stare at the tall white rocket.

A clock on the screen counts down. Ten. Nine. Eight.

Maya grips Oat's scaly leg. Oat's chest thumps.

Three. Two. One!

Flames burst from the base. Smoke spreads across the ground in a great gray cloud.

Then the sound strikes. It is not just loud — Maya can feel it in her chest! The grass trembles. Her teeth buzz.

Oat throws back his snout and roars. But nobody hears him. The rocket drowns out every other sound.

Up it climbs, a bright streak, up past the clouds, up until it is just a small spark.

"That," Maya says, still trembling, "was the best sound on Earth."

Oat grins. He thinks so too.","cover_scene":"A girl and a green dinosaur standing on grass watching a white rocket blast off with flames and billowing smoke clouds."}

{"title":"Maya's Bubble Rocket","level":3,"topic":"rockets","target_skill":"blends","text":"NASA has a plan for kids: build a bubble-powered rocket!

Oat stomps outside with a cup of water and a fizzy tablet.

"Let's try again!" Maya says. "This time I will make the tube more slim, so it splits the air faster."

{"title":"Maya the Star Astronaut","level":2,"topic":"astronauts","target_skill":"blends","text":"Maya wants to be an astronaut.

She puts on a white suit. She snaps the clasp. She grabs a glass helmet.

Oat helps her step up the tall ramp.

"Blast off!" Maya calls.

The ship climbs fast. Stars drift past the glass.

She plants a small flag. It stands stiff and still.

Oat stomps next to her. He drops a stone in her hand.

"A moon rock!" Maya gasps.

Then Mom calls, "Maya! Snack time!"

Maya blinks. She is in her room. Her helmet is a big bowl.

{"title":"The Blood Red Moon","level":3,"topic":"lunar eclipse","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":""Tonight the moon will glow blood red," Maya reads. "It is called a lunar eclipse."

She and Oat spread a quilt on the grass and wait. The air feels cool. Crickets creak in the weeds.

The moon sails up, round and cream white.

Then a dark shape creeps across it. Maya leans close.

"That is Earth's own shadow," she explains. "We are standing between the sun and the moon."

Slowly the shadow eats the moon. A bright sliver stays. Then even that fades.

Maya holds her breath.

The moon does not vanish. Instead it gleams a deep, dreamy red, like a coal in a fire.

"Sunlight sneaks around Earth and paints it," Maya whispers.

Oat leans his heavy head on the quilt and keeps staring.

They stay until dawn nears and the red fades away.

"Best night ever," Maya says.","cover_scene":"A girl and a green dinosaur on a quilt in the grass at night gazing up at a deep red moon in a starry sky."}
Noted.

{"title":"Oat Sees the Red Moon","level":2,"topic":"dinosaurs","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Oat wakes up at night. He sees the moon.

The moon is not white. It is red!

Oat runs to get Maya.

Maya rubs her eyes. "Oh! It is an eclipse," she says.

They sit on the grass. They lean on each other.

transcript.title: The Dino Team by the Sea
transcript.text:
Maya reads a big book about dinosaurs. The book says new facts are found each day!

She reads about a dino team by the sea. The team can leap and sail and float.

One dino eats green leaves. She has a long neck. She reaches up high to eat the leaves in the trees.

One dino likes to swim. He floats in the sea like a boat. His tail makes a big wave.

One dino has a sail on his back. It soaks up heat from the sun. Then he feels warm!

Rain falls on the sea. The dino team runs to a cave. They wait for the rain to stop.

Soon the sun peeks out. The team eats a meal of leaves and beans.

Maya shuts her book. "What a team!" she says. "I will read more each day."

chapters.title: The Dinosaur on the Trail
chapters.text:
Dean is a small dinosaur. He likes to eat green leaves by the stream.

One day, Dean sees a trail in the mud. The trail is deep and wide.

"Wait!" says Dean. "Who made this trail?"

Dean goes down the trail. He sees a green fern. He sees a goat on a boat. But no big dinosaur.

Rain falls. Dean gets wet. He hides in an oak tree and eats a leaf.

Then the ground shakes. Boom! Boom! A huge dinosaur walks by. Her neck is long. Her feet are the size of Dean!

"Do not be afraid," she says. "I eat leaves too."

Dean grins. "Can we eat as a team?"

"Yes!" she says.

They eat green leaves all day by the stream. Dean is glad he read the trail.

Real kids can read about dinosaurs too. Facts and games wait for you!

transcript.title: Rain on the Dino Trail
transcript.text:
Maya and Dad take a trail to the dino hall. New facts wait for them there!

Rain drips on the trail. Maya wears a coat. The rain makes a dark stain on the road.

In the hall, a big dino stands tall. Its tail is long. Its teeth are neat and sharp.

Maya reads the sign. "This dino ate meat. It ate a lot each day!"

Next, she sees a dino with a beak. It ate seeds and leaves. It made a nest and sat on eggs.

A man shows Maya a big bone. "Feel it," he says. The bone feels cold.

Maya draws a dino on a sheet. She paints it green with a red tail.

The rain ends. The sun beams on the road home.

"That was a great day!" Maya says. "Can we come again?"

Dad grins. "Yes. Soon."

chapters.title: Rain Day for the Green Dinosaur
chapters.text:
A big green dinosaur sat by the oak tree. She had to wait. The rain fell on her back.

"I need to eat," she said. "I will eat leaves."

She ate green leaves. Each leaf was wet with rain. Each leaf was sweet.

A goat came down the trail. The goat did not eat leaves. The goat ate oats.

"Wait for me!" said the goat. "Let us be a team."

So the dinosaur and the goat went up the trail. The rain fell. The leaves fell.

They ate on the trail. They ate in the rain. The goat ate oats. The dinosaur ate leaves.

Soon the rain went away. The sun came out. The trail was clean.

"That was a good meal," said the goat.

Maya can read about real dinosaurs, too. Kids can see dino facts and games and art. Real teams dig up dino bones each day!

transcript.title: The Dino Egg in the Oak Tree
transcript.text:
Maya finds a big egg near an oak tree. It is by the train track.

"Is it real?" she says. The egg has a crack.

Out pops a tiny dino! It has green skin and a long tail.

"I will call you Oat," Maya says.

Oat eats leaves from the oak tree. He eats beans. He eats a peach!

Maya reads a book to Oat. Facts about dinosaurs fill each page.

"Long ago, some dinos ate meat. Some ate seeds and leaves like you," she reads.

Oat needs a home. Maya makes a nest of hay near the road.

Rain falls. Oat sleeps in his nest. Maya keeps him dry with a coat.

In the morning, Oat is bigger! His feet are huge.

Maya gives a big squeal. "Soon you will not fit in this nest!"

Oat licks her cheek.

chapters.title: The Oak Tree Snack Team
chapters.text:
Rex is a small dinosaur. He sits by a big oak tree. He waits for his team.

"Wait for me!" calls Goat. Goat is not a dinosaur, but Goat is on the team.

Rex and Goat want to eat. They eat oats. They eat each leaf on the low branch. Each leaf is green and sweet.

Then rain! Rain taps the oak. Rain taps the oats. The team runs under the big oak tree.

"Wait," says Rex. "We can eat here!"

Goat eats oats. Rex eats a leaf. Each one gets a snack in the rain.

The rain stops. The oak drips. The team naps by the oak.

Scientists read about dinosaurs and find new facts each year. They tell us what dinosaurs ate: leaves, seeds, and more. Rex would say, "Eat each leaf! Wait for your team!"

Rain, oak, oats, leaf, team. Rex likes them all.

chapters.title: Sea Beach Dino Feast
chapters.text:
Dean is a big dino. Dean likes the sea.

Each day, Dean eats by the sea. He eats a leaf. He eats a heap of leaves!

"Eat with me!" Dean peeps.

A small dino runs to the beach. Her name is Bea. Bea can eat, eat, eat!

Dean and Bea are a team. The team leaps in the sea. The team naps in the heat.

Bea finds a green leaf. Dean finds a leaf. Each leaf is a treat!

"Eat up, team!" says Bea.

The sea is neat and clean. The dino team eats a big meal.

Real dinos are fun to read about. Kids can read dino facts and see dino art. Dinos ate leaves long, long ago!

Dean and Bea nap in the heat. Each dino has sweet dreams of leaves by the sea.

transcript.title: Oat Paints the Dino Road
transcript.text:
Maya has a plan. She will make a dino road!

She gets paint. Red paint. Gray paint. A pail of white paint too.

Oat helps. He dips his tail in the pail. Then he paints the road!

The road goes past the oak tree. It goes past the lake. It goes past the goat pen.

Maya nails a sign by the road. She reads it out loud. "Dino Road. Stay in your lane!"

Soon a toad hops on the road. A snail creeps on the road. The goat walks on the road.

"Wait!" Maya calls. "This road is for dinos!"

Oat gives a big roar. But then he smiles.

"You may all come," Maya says. "Dinos like to share."

So the toad and the snail and the goat ride on Oat's back, down the long gray road.

chapters.title: Dino Reads the Big Leaf Map
chapters.text:
Rex is a big green dino. Rex can read.

Today Rex will read a map. The map is on a leaf. A big flat leaf!

"Team! Come here!" Rex calls.

The team runs up. Stomp, stomp, stomp.

Rex reads the leaf map. "We will eat at the top of the hill."

The team likes to eat. Rex likes to eat. It is meal time!

Up they go. Rex holds the leaf map. The team reads it too.

At the top, they see a heap of green plants. What a meal!

Rex takes a leaf. Munch! The team takes a leaf. Munch, munch!

"This is the best meal," says Rex.

Then Rex reads one last bit of the leaf map. "Real dino facts are in books," he reads. "Kids can read them and see dino art!"

The team can eat. The team can read. Go, team!

transcript.title: Oat and the Deep Cave
transcript.text:
Maya reads a new dino fact. "Some bones hide in deep caves!"

"Let's go, Oat," she says.

They take the gray road. They pass the oak tree. They reach a deep cave by the sea.

Inside it is dim. Maya holds a light. Oat keeps close.

Drip. Drip. Water leaks from the peak of the cave.

Then Maya sees it. A huge bone in the clay!

"Wait," she says. "Is this real?"

She brushes the clay away. The bone is long and pale.

Oat sniffs it. He gives a soft moan.

"Do not be sad," Maya says. "This dino lived long ago. Now she can teach us."

They place the bone in a crate. They haul it up the trail.

At home, Maya makes a neat sign: MAYA'S BONE.

Oat beams. What a team!

chapters.title: Two Letters, One Sound: Dino's ea Rule
chapters.text:
Here is a rule. When e and a sit side by side, they make one sound. They say "ee." Just one sound. Not two.

Meet Pia. Pia is a dino. Pia can read.

Pia sees a leaf. Say it: l - ea - f. Leaf. One sound in the middle.

Pia can eat. Say it: ea - t. Eat. One sound.

Pia is on a team. Say it: t - ea - m. Team. One sound.

Now look at two words. Pat. Pan. Those have a short a. But heap has ea. Heap says "ee."

Sam the dino can not read yet. Sam says "e-a" as two sounds. Pia taps the word. "One sound, Sam!"

Sam tries. "Leaf. Eat. Team." Sam did it!

The team sits on the beach. They read dino facts and eat a big meal.

transcript.title: The Dino Fair on Main Street
transcript.text:
A dino fair comes to Main Street! Maya and Oat go at dawn.

Booths fill the street. One booth has dino art. One booth has games. One booth sells sweet treats.

Maya reads a fact card out loud. "New dino facts are found each year!"

At the first booth, Maya paints a dino. She paints it teal with a gold tail.

Oat waits by the treat cart. He wants a snack.

Maya buys him oats and a peach. Oat eats it all in one gulp!

Then a man calls, "Who can roar the best?"

What a neat day!

chapters.title: Dino Says It Slow
chapters.text:
Dino digs in the mud. He finds a big green l-ea-f. Say it slow: leef. Leaf!

Dino is not fast. Dino says it slow. That is a good trick.

Now Dino wants to e-a-t. Say it slow: eet. Eat!

He munches the leaf. Yum. His pals come to help.

Dino has a t-ea-m. Say it slow: teem. Team!

The team digs a deep pit. Dig, dig, dig!

In the pit is a bone. A real dino bone!

Dino wants to r-ea-d about it. Say it slow: reed. Read!

A kid book tells him facts. Nat Geo Kids has dino facts, games, and art. New facts come out all the time!

Dino grins. Slow is fine. Slow is smart.

Say it slow: leaf, eat, team, read.

You did it, just like Dino!

transcript.title: Oat and the Night Sky Dino
transcript.text:
Maya reads a new fact. "Some stars make shapes in the night sky!"

"Let's look, Oat," she says.

They wait for dark. They take a quilt to the green field by the oak tree.

The sky is deep blue. Then black. Stars peek out, one by one.

Maya sees three bright stars in a row. "That is a tail!" she says.

She traces more stars. A neck. A head. A row of teeth!

"Oat, it is a sky dino!"

Oat lifts his snout and gives a soft roar. The stars seem to gleam back.

A streak zooms past. A shooting star!

"Make a wish," Maya says.

She shuts her eyes tight. She wishes for more days like this one.

Oat leans close. Maya leans on his warm side.

Soon both of them sleep, under the sky dino.

chapters.title: Dino and the Great Track Trail
chapters.text:
Dino woke up on the grass. The sun was bright. Just then, he saw a track!

"A big track!" said Dino. "Let me read it. Tr-ack. Track!"

He took a step. Then a slow step. The trail went past a stump.

Gr-een grass. Gr-ay stone. St-ick. St-omp. Dino said each chunk slow, then fast.

"Sl-ow. Slow," said Dino. "I can say it!"

The trail went up a green hill. Dino ate a leaf on the way. He did not eat the whole tree!

At the top sat Stella. She had big feet and a long tail.

"You made this track!" said Dino.

"Just for fun," said Stella. "Now we are a team."

They sat in the grass and read a book of dino facts. Some dinos were as tall as trees! Some had teeth like sticks.

"Gr-eat book," said Dino. "Great!"

transcript.title: Oat and the Shell Shop
transcript.text:
Maya and Oat check the beach. They wish to find shells.

The shop by the dock sells dino things. A chart of dino facts hangs in the shop. Maya reads it. "New dino facts show up each year!"

"May we shop?" Maya asks.

The shop man grins. "Pick a thing that you wish for."

Maya picks a white shell. It has a shine like a tooth.

Oat shoves his snout in a dish of chips. Crunch! He chomps them all.

"Oat!" Maya says. "You must share!"

Oat shuts his mouth. He looks shy.

Then Oat digs in the sand with his chin. He finds a shell! It is thick and pink.

He puts it in Maya's hand.

"Thank you," Maya says. "This shell is the best."

They march home as the sun sinks.
transcript.cover_scene: A girl and a green dinosaur beside a small seaside shop filled with shells, the dinosaur nosing a thick pink shell into her hand.

chapters.title: Stella and the Stone Stump
chapters.text:
Stella the Stegosaurus stood by a stone stump at the edge of the stream. She had read that scientists still find new dinosaurs every year, and she wanted to find one too.

"St-ump," she said slowly. "Stump!" The stump was strong and old, and something was stuck under it.

Slim the Slothosaurus slid down the slope to help. "Sl-ow," he said. "Go slow, Stella."

Together they strained. Stomp, stomp! The stump moved. Under it lay a long, striped bone, still and cold.

"A strange bone!" said Slim. "Str-ong. Str-ipe. Str-ange!"

Stella stared. This bone did not match her team. It did not match Slim. It was a brand new dinosaur, sleeping under the stump for a million years.

They ran up the steep street of stones to tell the herd. Every dinosaur came to see.

"We found it," said Stella proudly. "Step by step, chunk by chunk, slow and strong."

chapters.title: Stego on Stone Street
chapters.text:
Stego was a strong stegosaurus with stiff plates down her spine. She lived near a steep slope at the end of Stone Street.

One still morning, Stego spotted a strange thing. A stack of straw sat on an old stump.

"St-ump," she said slowly. "Stump!"

She stepped closer and sniffed. Under the straw slept a small, striped baby dino. It slid out and blinked.

"Are you lost?" Stego asked.

The baby stood and stretched. It could not speak yet, so it just stamped its feet.

Stego let the baby stay close. They strolled down the street, past a stream and a strip of tall grass. Stego went slow so the baby could keep step.

At last, a big dino came stomping up the slope. The baby squealed and ran straight to her.

Scientists still study dinos like Stego. Brand new facts and art show us how strange and strong they were!

transcript.title: Oat Meets the Octopus
transcript.text:
Maya and Oat go to the fish tank hall.

A big glass tank shines. Maya puts her chin on the glass.

Then she sees it. An octopus! It has eight long arms.

"Wow!" Maya says. "It can shift its shape. It can squish in a thin gap!"

The octopus shoots past. It grabs a shell with one arm.

Oat taps the glass with his snout. The octopus turns pink!

Maya reads a chart on the wall. "Long ago, huge sea beasts swam here. Some had fins and sharp teeth. New facts come each year!"

She shows Oat a sketch of one. It looks much like a dino with flippers.

"You had cousins in the sea," she says.

Oat gives a soft huff.

The octopus waves one arm. Maya waves back.

"Thank you," she whispers. "What a day!"

chapters.title: Stripe the Shore Octopus
chapters.text:
Maya stood very still by the tide pool at the shore. Down in the cool water sat a small octopus with striped arms. Maya called him Stripe.

Stripe stretched one arm out slow, then slid it back. His arms were never stiff. He could squeeze through a slot no wider than a straw!

Maya said the tricky words the way she likes best: st-ood, stood. str-etched, stretched. sl-id, slid. Each chunk snapped together fast.

A sea turtle swam past the stones. Maya knew a fact about turtles: some turtles can stay under the water for hours while they sleep! Stripe stared at the turtle and turned a stony gray, just like the rock.

"You are a strong little star," Maya said.

Stripe stretched up one striped arm, almost like a wave goodbye. Then he slid under a stone and stayed still until the tide came back.

transcript.title: Five Sea Giants
transcript.text:
Maya sees a show. It tells about five huge beasts in the sea, long ago.

The first one has a long neck. It eats fish. It sails in the deep sea like a boat.

The next one has a wide tail. It beats the waves. It leaps and lands with a big splash.

The third one is a speedy one. It streaks past like a train. It reaches for a meal.

The fourth one has teeth like nails. Maya peeks from her seat. "Yikes!"

The last one is the biggest. It is as long as a road! Its jaw can eat a whole seal.

Maya reads the last screen. "These beasts lived in the sea. Each one was real!"

Oat leans on Maya.

"Do not be afraid," she says. "They swam here long ago."

chapters.title: Strong Streak the Sea Turtle
chapters.text:
Streak was a small sea turtle with one gold stripe on her shell. She wanted to swim to the far reef, but the waves were strong.

"Say it in chunks," said Mom. "str-ong. Strong. You are strong too."

Streak stretched her flippers. Str-etch. Stretch! She swam past a straw-thin eel and a string of shiny bubbles.

Near the rocks, a tiny fish was stuck in a strand of net. Streak did not stop. She pulled the strand straight until the little fish shot free.

"Thank you!" the fish said. "I hatched at a big aquarium in Chicago. People there raised a baby frogfish from an egg, the first time ever! Then they help us learn the sea."

Streak grinned. She swam down the reef street of coral, her gold stripe flashing.

Str-eak. Streak. A strong little turtle, strong all the way home.

"This tooth is real," he says. "It chomped fish!"

Maya wishes she could dig with him.

She grabs a dish and a brush. She digs in the sand patch.

Crunch! She finds a shell.

chapters.title: Shelly the Shy Shark
chapters.text:
Shelly was a shy shark who lived in a shady reef. She liked to hide in the thick kelp and watch the fish flash by.

One day, a thin fish named Thad swam up. "Shelly, will you show me the shell cave?" he asked.

Shelly shook her head. "I am too shy," she said.

Thad said, "Think of it like this. Say it in chunks: sh-ell. Shell! Now swim with me."

So Shelly swam. She dashed past a starfish and a strong stream of bubbles. The shell cave was full of shiny pink shells.

Then a dolphin splashed in to say hello. "Did you know dolphins are born tail-first?" she said. "We shoot out backward!"

Shelly laughed. "That is the best fact I ever heard!"

"Thank you for showing me the cave," said Thad.

Shelly smiled with all her teeth. A shy shark can still make three fine friends.

chapters.title: Swift the Frilly Seahorse
chapters.text:
Swift was a small seahorse with a frilly fin. He wanted to swim fast, but his tail kept curling around the fresh green weeds.

"Try chunking it," said Frida the fish. "Say sw-im. Swim!"

"Sw-im. Swim!" said Swift. He swished his frill and swam three quick loops.

A dolphin swept past with a sweep of her tail. "Did you know dolphins are born tail-first?" she said. "My tail came out before my nose!"

Swift laughed. "My tail is the best part of me too."

They swam to a sweet, fresh stream of bubbles near the shore. Frida showed Swift how to float still while the water swirled.

"Fr-ends. Friends," Swift said slowly. "Friends! That word is easy now."

The three of them swam home as the sun sank. Swift swished his frilly fin and thought, a swift tail is good, but fresh friends are better.

transcript.title: Tail First! A Dolphin Day
transcript.text:
Maya reads an amazing ocean fact out loud: "Dolphins are born tail first!"

"Tail first?" she says. "Let's go see, Oat."

They sail out in a small boat on a calm, gray sea. Oat keeps his snout low, waiting.

Soon a sleek dolphin leaps beside them, and then another. They squeak and chirp, speaking in sounds too high for Maya to hear.

One dolphin swims slowly near the boat. She is huge and round.

"Wait," Maya breathes. "I think she is a mom."

The sea churns. Then Maya sees it — a tiny tail! The baby slides out tail first, then floats up for its first gulp of air.

"That way it will not breathe too soon," Maya explains to Oat.

The team of dolphins sweeps away. Maya waves until they reach the deep.

"Best day at sea," she says.

chapters.title: Swoosh the Dolphin and the Swirling Tide
chapters.text:
Swoosh was a young dolphin with a smooth gray back. Did you know dolphins are born tail-first? Swoosh was, too! On his very first day, he swam beside his mother in the warm blue sea.

"Sw-im," his mother said. "Say it slow: s-w-im. Now swim!"

Swoosh swam. He swam past green weeds and a swaying sea fan. A swarm of tiny fish made a silver swirl around him.

Then the tide began to sweep. It swept sand up in a cloud. It swept a small crab off a rock!

Swoosh did not wait. He swished his tail and swooped down fast. He scooped the crab up on his nose and set him back on the rock.

"Thank you, swift one," said the crab.

Swoosh swelled with pride. He swam home through the swirling water, sweet and proud, ready to sweep the sea again tomorrow.

transcript.title: The Dolphin Who Knew Her Name
transcript.text:
Maya reads that each dolphin makes its own whistle soon after it is born. That whistle is like a name!

"Oat, they call each other by name," she says.

They row out at daybreak. The sea is clear and green.

A sleek dolphin appears. She squeaks and squawks. Then she leaps — so high she seems to hang in the air!

Another dolphin slaps its tail on the sea. Smack! Water sprays across the boat and soaks Oat's snout.

A third blows a stream of bubbles that float up like beads.

"They are speaking," Maya explains. "Leaping and slapping mean things too."

Maya cups her hands and makes her own sound — a long, low peep.

The first dolphin repeats it back, nearly the same!

Maya beams. "She learned my name."

Oat gives a deep roar, and the dolphins reply.

chapters.title: Crab Gram and the Green Reef Crew
chapters.text:
Gram was a gray crab with one proud claw. She lived by a green reef where the water was cool and clear.

"Swim with us!" cried the small fish. But Gram was slow. Crabs creep. They do not swim.

A gray dolphin named Prim swooped close. "I can teach you. When a word feels tricky, say it slow. S-w-im. Swim!"

Gram tried. "S-w-im. Swim!" Her claws swept the water. She began to swish along!

"Did you know dolphins are born tail-first?" grinned Prim. "We swim from the very first day."

Gram grinned back. She swam past green weeds. She swam through a swarm of tiny crabs who cheered from the sand.

A strong swirl of tide came. Gram did not freeze. She said it slow: "S-w-irl. Swirl." Then she rode it, proud and brave.

"Slow and strong wins," said Prim.

Gram waved her gray claw at the whole crew.

transcript.title: The Pod and the Bright Blue Net
transcript.text:
Maya learns that dolphins live in groups called pods. A baby dolphin is a calf, and it stays close to its mom.

She and Oat glide out in the small boat. A pod swims past, sleek and swift. They splash and spin and slap their tails.

"Dolphins are not fish," Maya tells Oat. "They are mammals, like us. They breathe air."

A dolphin clicks. The sound streams out, strikes a stone, and skips back. That is how she finds her food in the gloom.

Then Maya spots trouble. A bright blue net drifts near the pod! A small calf swims straight at it.

"Stop!" Maya cries.

Oat plunges in. He grips the net with his strong snout and drags it free.

The calf twists away and spins with glee.

The pod claps the sea with their flippers. Splash! Splash! Splash!

chapters.title: Grace the Green Sea Turtle and the Strong Tide
chapters.text:
Grace was a green sea turtle with a proud, strong shell. Say it slow: s-t-r-ong. Strong!

One bright day, Grace swam past a crab named Cleo. "Say it slow," Grace grinned. "s-w-am. Swam!"

Cleo crept out from a crack in the gray rock. "c-r-ept. Crept!" she cried. "A strong tide is pulling my friends from the reef!"

Grace did not freeze. She swept her front flippers and swam into the swirl. "s-w-irl. Swirl!"

The tide was strong, but Grace was stronger. She pressed on, past drifting grass and a swarm of small fish. "s-w-arm. Swarm!"

One by one, she brought her friends back: three crabs, a prawn, and a frog fish. "p-r-awn. Prawn! f-r-og. Frog!"

Cleo clapped her claw. "c-l-aw. Claw!"

Here is a true fact: sea turtles can swim across a whole ocean. Grace was proud. Say it slow: p-r-oud. Proud!

transcript.title: Oat and the Rocket Roar
transcript.text:
Maya learns a loud fact: a rocket blasting off is louder than thunder!

"Let's go, Oat," she says. They stand on the grass and stare at the tall white rocket.

A clock on the screen counts down. Ten. Nine. Eight.

Maya grips Oat's scaly leg. Oat's chest thumps.

Three. Two. One!

Flames burst from the base. Smoke spreads across the ground in a great gray cloud.

Then the sound strikes. It is not just loud — Maya can feel it in her chest! The grass trembles. Her teeth buzz.

Oat throws back his snout and roars. But nobody hears him. The rocket drowns out every other sound.

Up it climbs, a bright streak, up past the clouds, up until it is just a small spark.

"That," Maya says, still trembling, "was the best sound on Earth."

Oat grins. He thinks so too.

chapters.title: Maya's Rocket Ride to the Quiet Side of Space
chapters.text:
Maya made a rocket from a big tube and tape. She gave it a name: Brave.

"It is time," she said. "Time to ride!"

Say it slow: t-i-me. The e is quiet, so the i says its name. Time. Ride. Brave.

The rocket shook. Flames made a bright line, and up it rose into space.

Maya could see the whole blue globe below her. Nine white clouds. One wide sea.

"Here is the Moon," she said. Say it slow: h-ere. Here!

She drove past a stone the size of a home. She wrote a note on her slate: "Space is a quiet place."

At NASA, kids can build a bubble-powered rocket and see how high it will go. Maya plans to make five more when she lands.

"Same time next week, Brave," she said. "Now take me home."

Down, down, down. Safe. Home.

transcript.title: Maya's Bubble Rocket
transcript.text:
NASA has a plan for kids: build a bubble-powered rocket!

Maya grabs a stiff sheet of paper and a small plastic tube. She rolls the paper into a slim tube and tapes it.

Oat stomps outside with a cup of water and a fizzy tablet.

Maya drops the tablet in, snaps on the cap, and stands the rocket on the flat stone.

They wait. Inside, the tablet spits and froths. Bubbles press and press against the cap.

POP! The rocket blasts straight up, past the fence, past the branch, almost to the clouds!

Oat's jaw drops.

The rocket drifts down and plops in the grass.

"Let's try again!" Maya says. "This time I will make the tube more slim, so it splits the air faster."

Oat stamps his feet. He cannot wait.

chapters.title: The Bubble Rocket at Base Nine
chapters.text:
Maya had a plan. She would make a bubble rocket, just like the one NASA shows kids on its space page. Fizzy bubbles push. The push sends the rocket up!

"What is your rocket's n-a-me?" asked Dad. Maya grinned. "Its name is Base Nine."

She taped the fins. She shook the tube. Then she set it on a flat stone in the yard.

"It is t-i-me," Maya said. "Time to launch!"

POP! Base Nine shot up past the white clouds. Maya had to be br-a-ve to watch it climb so high. Brave Maya did not blink.

Up in sp-a-ce, the stars looked like bright chips of glass. Space is wide and quiet and cold.

Then the rocket slid back down and landed in the grass.

"Time to go h-o-me," Dad said.

Maya smiled. Home, then a new plan. Next time, she made a note, Base Ten will fly.

transcript.title: Maya the Star Astronaut
transcript.text:
Maya wants to be an astronaut.

She puts on a white suit. She snaps the clasp. She grabs a glass helmet.

Oat helps her step up the tall ramp.

"Blast off!" Maya calls.

The ship climbs fast. Stars drift past the glass.

Soon Maya floats! Her braid stands up. Her snack drifts by. She grins and spins.

The ship stops by the moon. Maya steps out on the gray dust.

Stomp! Her boot prints stay in the dust.

She plants a small flag. It stands stiff and still.

Oat stomps next to her. He drops a stone in her hand.

"A moon rock!" Maya gasps.

Then Mom calls, "Maya! Snack time!"

Maya blinks. She is in her room. Her helmet is a big bowl.

But the stone is still in her hand.

chapters.title: Maya and the Nine Moon Clocks
chapters.text:
Maya's job on the moon base was to fix the clocks. Her n-a-me was on every one. Nine clocks. Nine ticks. "My name is on clock nine!" she said.

Each clock told the t-i-me back on Earth. Time for lunch. Time to sleep. Time to call h-o-me.

But clock nine had stopped. Maya pulled her tools from the b-a-se of the shelf. She m-a-de a new spring from bright wire and slid it in. Tick! Tick!

"Good work," said Chan. "Come watch the sky. Scientists say a big new telescope, called Roman, will launch soon to hunt strange planets. Some are so puffy they are less thick than cotton candy!"

transcript.title: The Blood Red Moon
transcript.text:
"Tonight the moon will glow blood red," Maya reads. "It is called a lunar eclipse."

She and Oat spread a quilt on the grass and wait. The air feels cool. Crickets creak in the weeds.

The moon sails up, round and cream white.

Then a dark shape creeps across it. Maya leans close.

"That is Earth's own shadow," she explains. "We are standing between the sun and the moon."

Slowly the shadow eats the moon. A bright sliver stays. Then even that fades.

Maya holds her breath.

The moon does not vanish. Instead it gleams a deep, dreamy red, like a coal in a fire.

"Sunlight sneaks around Earth and paints it," Maya whispers.

Oat leans his heavy head on the quilt and keeps staring.

They stay until dawn nears and the red fades away.

"Best night ever," Maya says.

chapters.text:
Maya put on her space suit and climbed into the ship. "My n-a-me, name, is Maya," she said, "and it is t-i-me, time, to fly!"

Scientists found strange new planets called super-puffs. They are so light and fluffy that they feel like cotton candy! Maya wanted to see one.

The ship left home and sped past nine bright stars. N-i-ne, nine, stars, all in a line! Maya made a chart. She m-a-de, made, a dot for each one.

Then she saw it: a huge puff planet, pink as candy floss. It had no hard stone, just soft haze.

"This is the best place in space," Maya said. She spoke to her b-a-se, base, on the radio. The crew at b-a-se, base, cheered.

Maya turned the ship for h-o-me, home. Same time, same place, next week!

"H-o-me, home," she smiled. "But space knows my name now."

transcript.title: Oat Sees the Red Moon
transcript.text:
Oat wakes up at night. He sees the moon.

The moon is not white. It is red!

Oat runs to get Maya.

Maya rubs her eyes. "Oh! It is an eclipse," she says.

They sit on the grass. They lean on each other.

"Do not be afraid," Maya says. "Earth made a big shade on the moon."

"The sun beams past Earth. The light turns red. It paints the moon red."

Oat peeks up. The red moon gleams.

"Long ago, dinosaurs saw this too," Maya says. "They sat and looked up, just like us."

Oat gives a soft roar.

Soon the shade creeps away. The moon is white again.

Maya yawns. "Time to sleep."

Oat leans down. Maya sleeps on his warm side, deep in a dream.

Maya made a line on her pad. L-i-ne. Line! She made a dot for the red moon.

"Take my place," said Sam. "P-l-a-ce. Place!"

The red moon sat in space. S-p-a-ce. Space!

"Same moon," said Maya. "New shade. What a fine, fine night!"

transcript.title: Oat Digs Up a New Dinosaur
transcript.text:
Big news! A new dinosaur was found!

Maya reads it out loud. "Kids can hunt for bones too."

"Let's dig, Oat!" she says.

They take a pail and a spade to the hill by the road.

Oat digs with his feet. Dirt sprays. Maya digs with her hands.

Clink! Maya's spade hits something hard.

She sweeps the dirt away. A bone! It is long and gray.

Then she finds three more. And a tooth as big as her shoe!

"Oat, this dinosaur ate meat," she says. "Look at that tooth."

They load the bones in the pail. They haul it down the trail.

A lady at the museum beams. "This is a real find!"

She puts the bones on a stand. She makes a sign.

The sign reads: FOUND BY MAYA AND OAT.

chapters.title: Maya and the Sea of Rain
chapters.text:
Maya sees a big gray spot on the moon. It has a name. It is the Sea of Rain! But it is not a real sea. No waves. No boats. Just dust.

"I will go," says Maya. "I will sail to the moon."

Her ship lifts off in a streak of heat. She floats. She waves at Earth.

Maya lands on the gray plain. She takes a deep breath. She reads a sign she made: S-e-a of R-ai-n.

"Let me teach you," she says to Bean, her cat. "Say it slow. R-ai-n. Rain!"

Bean naps on a stone.

Far off, a new space eye sails up. It is real! NASA will send it to seek stars. Its name is Roman.

Maya waves. "Go seek, Roman! I will keep the Sea of Rain safe."

Then she goes h-o-me for tea.

transcript.title: Grandpa and the Dinosaur Hall
transcript.text:
Grandpa takes Maya to the dinosaur hall. Oat waits by the gate.

The main room is huge. A long tail hangs over their heads.

"That one ate leaves," Grandpa says. "It had a neck like a crane."

Maya reads each sign out loud. She learns three new facts.

One: some dinosaurs had feathers.

Two: some had beaks like birds.

Three: new kinds are found each year!

They see a nest with eggs. They see claws. They see teeth in a row.

Grandpa points at a small dino near the door. It has green skin and a long tail.

"Hey," he says. "That one looks like Oat!"

Maya grins. "It sure does."

At the shop, Grandpa buys her a toy dino and a book.

On the way home, Maya reads the whole book out loud.

chapters.title: The Dino Who Loved the Sea
chapters.text:
Maya met a small dino named Teal.

Teal did not like to sleep. Teal liked the sea.

"Can you teach me to swim?" Teal said.

"Yes!" said Maya. "But first, say it slow. s-ea. Sea!"

Teal said it fast. Sea!

They ran to the beach. Big boats sat on the waves. Say it slow: b-oa-ts. Boats!

Teal did not float at first. Teal sank like a stone. But Maya held his tail.

Soon Teal could swim! He swam past the boats. He swam to the reef.

Then a big drop fell. Then ten more. R-ai-n. Rain!

"Rain is fine," said Teal. "I am wet! I am in the sea!"

They sat on the sand and ate a snack.

Maya read a real fact to Teal: long ago, big beasts did swim in the sea!

"That was me," said Teal. "That was my team."

transcript.title: Oat and the Feather Trail
transcript.text:
Maya reads a new fact. "Some dinosaurs had feathers!"

Oat blinks. He feels his own back. Just green skin.

"Do not be sad," Maya says. "Let's go look for feathers."

They take the trail by the oak tree. The day is clear and warm.

Maya sees a gray feather in the weeds. She picks it up.

Oat sees a brown one near the stream. He scoops it up with his snout.

Soon the pail is full. Red ones. Blue ones. One big white one!

At home, Maya gets tape. She sticks each feather on a sheet.

Then she tapes the sheet to Oat's back.

Oat turns. He sees the feathers. He leaps and flaps!

He cannot fly. But he beams.

"Now you look just like your great, great grandpa," Maya says.

chapters.title: Teal the Dino and the Rain Boat
chapters.text:
Teal is a small dino. T-ea-l. Teal! Her tail is green and gold.

One day, big drops fall. R-ai-n. Rain! Rain taps on the leaves.

"I can not swim in this," says Teal. "I need a boat." B-oa-t. Boat!

Teal drags a log to the sea. S-ea. Sea! The log floats. F-l-oa-ts. Floats!

Teal sits. Her tail is the sail. T-ai-l. Tail! S-ai-l. Sail!

The rain stops. Big beasts wave from the beach. B-ea-sts. Beasts! They are her pals.

"Teach us!" they squeak. T-ea-ch. Teach!

So Teal makes ten small boats. Ten beasts sail on the sea.

At home, Maya reads about real dinos. Scientists dig up bones and learn new facts each week.

Maya grins. "I can read teal, rain, and boat fast now!"

And she can.

transcript.title: T. Rex and the Big Roar
transcript.text:
Maya paints a T. rex on a big sheet.

She paints the teeth first. Each tooth is the size of a peach!

Then she paints two tiny arms. "Sorry," she says. "That is how they were."

Oat peeks at the paint. He makes a soft moan.

"Are you afraid?" Maya asks. "Do not be. T. rex lived long, long ago."

She reads a fact to him. "T. rex could eat meat in huge bites. But new facts show it was a mom too. It made a nest and kept its eggs safe."

Oat leans near the sheet.

Maya tapes it on the wall by her bed.

"Sleep well," she says to the T. rex.

That night she dreams. She rides on a T. rex down a long green road, and Oat leads the way.

chapters.title: Maya Digs Up a Giant
chapters.text:
Maya got a pail and a big coat. Today she digs for bones!

The dig site is near a road. Dust floats. Maya kneels on the clay.

Tap, tap. She sees a shape. Say it slow: b-o-ne. Bone!

"This is a r-ea-l bone," she says. "Real!"

She brushes the dirt. She sees a big t-ai-l. Tail! Then a long neck. Then teeth!

"T. rex!" Maya beats her fists in the air. T. rex teeth are like nails.

A man helps her lift each bone. They load them on a truck. The road is long, but Maya grins.

At the hall, the team sets each bone in place. The T. rex stands so tall! Maya has to crane her neck.

She reads a book of dino facts. Say it slow: l-ea-rn. Learn!

"I will l-ea-rn it all," Maya says. "Dinos are the b-ea-st of beasts!"

transcript.title: Oat Leads the Way Home
transcript.text:
Maya and Oat hike far up the trail. Too far!

The sun sinks. The road home is gone.

"Oh no," Maya says. "Which way?"

Oat lifts his snout. He sniffs the air. He sniffs the leaves. He sniffs the damp road dust.

Then he roars. He has the scent!

"Oat leads!" Maya says.

Oat leads her past the oak tree. Oat leads her past the goat pen. Oat leads her past the deep green lake.

Rain starts. Maya pulls up her coat. Oat keeps his nose low.

At last Maya sees it. A light! Home!

Mom waits at the door. "There you are!"

Maya reads Oat a book by the fire. She reads about a dino who saves the day.

"That dino is you," she says.

Oat yawns and sleeps.

chapters.title: The Dig Team's Big Coat Day
chapters.text:
Maya put on her c-oa-t. Coat! The air was cold at the dig.

"Load up the truck," said Nate. L-oa-d. Load!

Maya had a pail of n-ai-ls. Nails! They held the crates shut.

She took the dirt road to the site. R-oa-d. Road!

Maya likes to l-ea-rn. Learn! She r-ea-ds. Reads! She reads about big b-ea-sts. Beasts!

Long ago, real beasts ate leaves near this place. Some had a tail like a whip.

Maya dug. Tap, tap. She saw a bone in the clay.

They wrapped it up. Maya held it close in her coat.

On the way home, rain hit the road. Maya did not mind.

transcript.title: Oat and the Dinosaur Quiz Show
transcript.text:
A dinosaur quiz show comes to Maya's school. Teams answer questions about creatures that roamed the Earth long ago.

Maya and Oat join the green team.

"Question one," says the host. "Which dinosaur had plates along its back?"

Maya's hand shoots up. "Stegosaurus!"

Ding! One point.

"Question two. What did the long-necked ones eat?"

"Leaves!" Maya calls. "They reached high into the treetops."

Ding! Two points.

The red team streaks ahead. Maya's cheeks feel hot.

"Last question," the host says. "How do we learn new dinosaur facts each year?"

Maya freezes. Her mind is blank.

Then Oat stomps his foot. He scrapes the floor with his claw, as if digging.

"Digging!" Maya shouts. "Scientists dig up bones and teeth, and each new find teaches us something!"

Ding! The green team wins!

Oat lifts Maya onto his back, and the whole room cheers.

chapters.title: The Stone That Kept a Secret
chapters.text:
Maya hiked up to the dig site at sunrise. The air was cool and the trail was steep.

"Say it slow," said Coach Ray. "s-i-te. Site!"

Maya knelt close to a wide gray stone. She could see a shape inside it, like a hidden bone.

"b-o-ne. Bone!" she said. "A whole bone, not just a chip!"

She used a fine brush and made each stroke slow. Dust rose. The stone began to split.

Inside lay a long, curved tail bone. It was the size of her arm.

"Is it real?" Maya said.

"r-ea-l. Real," Coach Ray smiled. "Real and rare."

They wrapped it in tape and drove the crate home before the rain came.

That night Maya read on National Geographic Kids that new dinosaur facts are found each year by people just like her.

She closed the page, but she did not close her eyes.

She made a plan to dig again at dawn.

transcript.title: The Dinosaur Who Painted
transcript.text:
Maya's class must make art for the school fair. Maya groans. "I cannot draw," she says.

Oat nudges the paint trays with his snout.

"You want to help?" Maya asks.

Oat dips his tail in the teal paint. He sweeps it across a huge sheet. A long streak appears — clean and curved, like an ocean wave.

Maya laughs. "Keep going!"

Oat dips his claw in green and makes leaves. He dips his nose in gray and dots the clouds.

Maya paints too. She adds a beach, a boat, and three dolphins leaping.

At the fair, people crowd around their sheet.

"Who painted this?" a teacher asks.

"We both did," Maya says. "A team."

They win a bright blue ribbon.

On the way home, Oat carries it in his teeth the whole way, beaming.

chapters.title: The Bone Cave at Pine Ridge
chapters.text:
Maya woke at sunrise and hiked up Pine Ridge with her dig team. Deep in the rock, a cave had opened wide.

"A new site!" she said. "s-i-te. Site."

Inside, one huge stone held a shape. Maya knelt and brushed the grit away. A bone! "b-o-ne. Bone," she said slowly. "Not bon. Bone. The e at the end makes the o say its name."

The whole team leaned close. "Is it real?" asked Joe.

"r-ea-l. Real," Maya said. "And it is fine work. Something this size came from a giant."

They wrapped each piece and placed it in a crate. Rain tapped the cave roof while they wrote every fact on a clean page.

Back home, Maya read about dinosaurs on National Geographic Kids. Scientists there share news, art, and games about these amazing animals.

"Someday," Maya said, "my cave bone will be on a page like this."

transcript.title: Oat and the Winter Fossil Hunt
transcript.text:
Snow covers the hillside where Maya and Oat once dug for bones.

"Nothing to find today," Maya sighs. "It is all buried."

But Oat snorts and swings his tail. Whoosh! The snow flies off in a sparkling cloud.

Underneath, the frozen ground is scattered with smooth pebbles — and something else.

Maya kneels. A curved ridge pokes through the dirt. She scrapes gently with her glove.

"Oat," she breathes. "It is a claw."

It is longer than her whole hand, sharp as a hook.

They wrap it in Maya's scarf and carry it to the museum. The scientist turns it over carefully under a lamp.

"Remarkable," she says. "Scientists discover new dinosaur facts every single year, and this claw will teach us more."

Maya glows the entire walk home.

Oat walks proudly beside her, leaving enormous footprints in the snow.

chapters.title: Maya and the Spine Stone
chapters.text:
Maya woke before the sun and rode out to the dig site. Say it slow: s-i-te. Site.

A huge pine tree stood close to the trail, and under it lay a stone with a strange shape.

"That stone has a spine in it," said Dr. Reed. "A whole row of spikes!"

Maya knelt and brushed the grit away. The bone did not hide. It rose up like a wave. Say it slow: sh-a-pe. Shape.

She wrote in her notebook, page after page. Say it slow: p-a-ge. Page.

"Kids read dinosaur news online," Dr. Reed said. "Soon they will read about this one."

Maya smiled. The huge stone spine had waited a long, long time. Now it came home in a crate.

She closed her notebook. One more line, in her best hand: A fine day. A whole spine. Maya was here.
